PAR combines multi-scale downsampling, an autoregressive transformer for conditional embeddings, and a flow-based backbone decoder (Figure 1).
PAR addresses autoregressive exposure bias with noisy context learning and scheduled sampling (Section 3).

On unconditional backbone generation, PAR is evaluated against FrameDiff, RFDiffusion, ESM3, Genie2, and Proteina using designability, FPSD/fS, diversity, novelty, and secondary-structure metrics (Table 1).
PAR demonstrates zero-shot generalization to human-prompted conditional generation and motif scaffolding without fine-tuning (Section 4.2).
Combining SDE and ODE sampling across scales yields a 2.5x inference speedup over the single-scale 400-step baseline (Table 2).

zAl9heLw4q.text: Motive computes motion-specific data attribution by applying motion-weighted loss masks so gradients emphasize dynamic regions rather than static appearance (Section 3.4).
The method includes a video-specific frame-length bias fix to reduce spurious attribution to longer clips (Section 3.3).
Fine-tuning on Motive-selected data improves VBench motion smoothness and dynamic degree over baselines while using only a fraction of the training data (Table 1).
Human evaluation reports a 74.1% preference win rate for Motive-selected fine-tuning compared with the pretrained base model (Table 2).

eXxFlOPTk4.text: VideoKR contains 315K video reasoning examples over 145K newly collected CC-licensed expert-domain videos (Section 3.1).
The data pipeline uses human-curated seed examples, skill-oriented generation, and filtering intended to remove examples solvable from text or a few frames (Sections 3.3-3.5).
VideoKR-Eval is constructed to reduce single-frame shortcut answerability found in existing knowledge-intensive video benchmarks (Table 2).
SFT plus RL post-training on VideoKR improves knowledge-intensive video reasoning averages for Qwen2.5-VL-7B and Qwen3-VL-8B compared with their base models (Table 3).
Ablations indicate that adding knowledge-enhanced perception and complex reasoning examples improves VideoKR-Eval and knowledge-intensive benchmark performance (Table 4).

t73XUJvyQr.text: LLapDiff models irregular targets as low-dimensional latent trajectories, enabling horizon-wide generation without numerical integration over physical time (Section 4.4).
The denoiser parameterizes mean evolution in the Laplace domain with stable complex-conjugate poles for direct evaluation at irregular timestamps (Section 4.2).
A renewal-averaging analysis maps irregular sampling gaps to effective event-domain poles and motivates gap-aware history conditioning (Section 4.3).
Across seven real-world datasets, LLapDiff reports the strongest long-horizon probabilistic forecasting results on the main CRPS/MSE comparison (Table 1).
The same queried latent-trajectory model performs missing-value imputation by querying historical timestamps without retraining (Figure 3).

3BW15kSPfN.text: h1 synthesizes long-horizon reasoning examples by chaining existing short-horizon GSM8K-style problems without new human or teacher-model annotations (Section 3).
The training recipe uses outcome-only RL with a curriculum that automatically increases composed problem horizon length (Section 3).
Curriculum RL on composed sixth-grade math problems boosts accuracy on GSM-Symbolic, MATH-500, and AIME by up to 2.06x (Table 1).
Models trained with h1 transfer to out-of-distribution ReasoningGym domains and long-context benchmarks (Table 2).
The analysis claims curriculum RL gives an exponential sample-complexity improvement over full-horizon training in a simplified long-horizon skills model (Section 6).

pZNo1YWT5x.text: XDLM unifies masked and uniform-noise discrete diffusion through a stationary noise kernel that recovers MDLM and UDLM as limiting cases (Section 3.1).
An algebraic scalar reformulation of posterior and KL terms reduces memory and computation for large-vocabulary XDLM training (Section 3.2).
XDLM surpasses UDLM by 5.4 points on averaged zero-shot language benchmarks after OpenWebText training (Table 1).
In few-step conditional image generation, XDLM reduces FID from MDLM's 80.8 to 54.1 at 4 steps (Table 3).
When applied to an 8B LLaDA model, LLaDA-XDLM reaches 15.0 MBPP at 32 sampling steps, more than doubling the base LLaDA score (Table 16).

mWxEAgz3xu.text: The study surveys 306 practitioners and conducts 20 in-depth production-agent case-study interviews across 26 domains (Section 3).
For deployed agents, 68% execute at most ten autonomous steps before requiring human intervention (Figure 8).
Seventy percent of the detailed production case studies rely on off-the-shelf models without SFT or RL weight tuning (Figure 6).
Human-in-the-loop evaluation is the dominant evaluation mode for deployed agents, used by 74.2% of surveyed deployed systems (Figure 10).
Reliability is identified as the top development challenge for production agents, ahead of latency and security constraints (Figure 11).

lK2o9OjoXf.text: Plantain trains models to interleave planning, private reasoning, and visible answers instead of using a think-then-answer format (Section 3).
The first visible intermediate response in Plantain is an explicit step-by-step plan intended to allow early user feedback (Section 3).
Plantain reports about a 6% pass@1 improvement across the evaluated math reasoning and coding benchmarks (Table 1).
Plantain reduces time-to-first-response by over 60% relative to think-then-answer baselines while preserving final-answer quality trends (Table 1).
Ablations compare plan-first interleaving against other interleaving strategies and report plan-first as the strongest configuration (Table 3).

Ws8swqL5ob.text: PhotoAgent formulates autonomous image editing as long-horizon decision-making with tree search, memory, visual feedback, and closed-loop execution (Section 3).
UGC-Edit contains 7,000 real user photos annotated with human aesthetic scores and is used to train an aesthetic reward model (Section 5.1).
The end-to-end editing benchmark contains 1,017 real-world photographs across portraits, landscapes, urban scenes, food, objects, and low-light imagery (Section 5.2).
PhotoAgent reports state-of-the-art results across quantitative metrics, qualitative assessment, and user studies on the 1,017-photo benchmark (Table 2).
Ablations attribute performance gains to exploratory long-horizon planning for multi-round aesthetic optimization (Section 5.4).

hCAEcqig2C.text: The paper formalizes randomized self-reduction learning and provides sample-complexity analysis under correlated sampling (Section 4).
RSR-Bench contains 80 benchmark functions for evaluating randomized self-reduction discovery (Section 5).
Vanilla Bitween discovers randomized self-reductions for 43 of 80 RSR-Bench functions, including the first known sigmoid reduction (Table 1).
Agentic Bitween discovers randomized self-reductions for 64 of 80 RSR-Bench functions by letting LLM agents propose query functions beyond the fixed prior query set (Table 1).
On nonlinear invariant benchmarks, the regression backend outperforms the MILP backend in sample count and runtime (Table 2).

fdkSA4F0lN.text: Weak diffusion priors can match strong-prior inverse-problem baselines when measurements are highly informative, such as many observed pixels (Table 1).
The theory gives conditions under which high-dimensional measurements make the Bayesian posterior concentrate near the true signal despite weak priors (Theorem 3.1).
Local-correlation analysis argues that weak and stronger natural-image priors can share spatial structure useful for reconstruction (Table 2).
Cross-domain experiments evaluate weak priors from domain mismatch and low-fidelity generators across inverse-problem tasks (Section 4.2).
The paper identifies failure regimes for weak priors, including box inpainting and large-scale super-resolution where strong priors remain important (Figure 3).

7pQIzVNctu.text: Rex converts explicit Runge-Kutta and stochastic Runge-Kutta schemes into algebraically reversible exponential solvers for diffusion ODEs and SDEs (Section 3).
The ODE Rex construction inherits arbitrary order of convergence and a non-zero linear stability region from the base McCallum-Foster method (Theorem A.1).
Rex achieves near-machine-precision reconstruction under exact inversion in image-generation inversion experiments (Figure 7).
Rex improves or remains competitive on unconditional generation, text-conditioned generation, and image editing benchmarks versus prior reversible solvers (Figures 7-9).
Rex enables accurate likelihood-based Boltzmann sampling on tri-alanine with flow models (Table 1).

EeuLO2BjFN.text: MaxRL defines a compute-indexed family of sample-based objectives that interpolates between standard RL and exact maximum likelihood as sampling compute increases (Abstract).
The MaxRL objectives admit a simple unbiased policy-gradient estimator for non-differentiable sampling settings (Abstract).
The paper claims MaxRL converges to maximum-likelihood optimization in the infinite-compute limit (Abstract).
Empirically, MaxRL Pareto-dominates tested existing methods across all evaluated models and tasks (Abstract).
MaxRL reports up to 20x test-time scaling efficiency gains compared with a GRPO-trained counterpart (Abstract).

h7WBYYJF1Q.text: The paper connects recurrent-depth language models to diffusion language models and uses this connection to motivate a diffusion forcing sampler (Section 3).
The sampler decodes new tokens every forward pass while refining latent states for those tokens in parallel through recurrent depth (Section 3.1).
The paper proves the sampler is strictly more expressive than baseline autoregressive generation under the same time budget on modern hardware (Theorem 4.2).
The diffusion forcing sampler applies directly to existing 3.5B recurrent-depth transformers without tuning (Section 5).
Experiments report around 5x generation speedups with roughly 1% quality trade-offs depending on task and hyperparameters (Table 1).

kR4iOTaAOJ.text: ThunderAgent abstracts agentic workflows as LLM Programs that unify KV cache, system state, and external tool resources (Section 3).
The system adds a program-aware scheduler to improve KV cache hit rates and reduce memory imbalance across agent workflows (Section 4.2).
The tool resource manager asynchronously prepares and reuses tool environments, including disk and port resources (Section 4.3).
ThunderAgent reports 1.5-3.6x serving throughput improvements over state-of-the-art inference systems (Figure 5).
ThunderAgent reports 1.8-3.9x RL rollout speedups and up to 4.2x disk memory savings (Figures 6 and 9).

PnTXyTR2VG.text: LatentLM represents continuous modalities with VAE latents and uses next-token diffusion for autoregressive generation of those latent vectors (Section 2).
The proposed sigma-VAE is designed to prevent variance collapse in continuous latent tokenization for autoregressive modeling (Section 2.3).
On ImageNet image generation, LatentLM reports competitive or better FID than Diffusion Transformer baselines with stronger scaling trends (Table 1 and Figure 4).
In multimodal large-language-model experiments, LatentLM outperforms vector-quantized models and Transfusion on scaling curves for text-to-image and image-to-text generation (Figure 8).
For zero-shot text-to-speech on LibriSpeech test-clean, LatentLM outperforms VALL-E 2 in speaker similarity and robustness while using far fewer autoregressive decoding steps (Table 4).

PeFSCRulgy.text: TerminalTraj filters repositories to construct Dockerized execution environments, generates Docker-aligned task instances, and synthesizes executable validated terminal trajectories (Abstract).
TerminalTraj curates 32K Docker images and generates 50,733 verified terminal trajectories across eight domains (Abstract).
Models trained on TerminalTraj with a Qwen2.5-Coder backbone report gains up to 20% on TerminalBench 1.0 and 10% on TerminalBench 2.0 over their backbones (Abstract).
TerminalTraj-32B reaches 35.30% on TB 1.0 and 22.00% on TB 2.0 among models with fewer than 100B parameters (Abstract).
The paper claims TerminalTraj-32B improves test-time scaling behavior on terminal-agent benchmarks (Abstract).

vTp9JToZl9.text: The paper identifies Cross-Modal Entropy Collapse as a failure mode caused by hard projection of sparse point clouds onto image-plane grids (Section 1).
SplAttN replaces hard projection with Differentiable Gaussian Splatting to create a dense continuous image-plane representation for 2D-3D fusion (Section 3.3).
SplAttN achieves state-of-the-art average Chamfer Distance on the PCN point-cloud completion benchmark (Table 1).
SplAttN reports best F1 score and lowest average Chamfer Distance on ShapeNet-34/21 seen and unseen splits (Table 3).
KITTI counterfactual evaluation shows SplAttN remains dependent on visual cues while baselines behave like unimodal template retrievers (Figure 8).

3gCdh3u2GK.text: Mind-Omni unifies seven brain, image, and text encoding/decoding tasks in a single discrete diffusion framework (Table 1).
The Brain Tokenizer converts continuous fMRI signals into discrete tokens aligned with image and text representations in a shared semantic space (Section 3.1).
The framework curates a Brain Question Answering instruction-tuning dataset using Qwen2-VL to support reasoning over brain signals (Section 4).
Mind-Omni establishes a new state of the art among unified brain-vision-language frameworks in the multi-task evaluation (Tables 2-4).
Joint image-text conditioning shows synergistic gains over single-modality conditioning in neural encoding and decoding analyses (Figures 7 and 8).

lwOoBzJykL.text: LaST0 represents future visual dynamics, 3D structure, and robot proprioceptive states as a token-efficient latent spatio-temporal chain of thought (Section 3).
The architecture uses a Mixture-of-Transformers design with a low-frequency reasoning expert and a high-frequency acting expert (Section 3.4).
LaST0 achieves a 98.1% mean success rate on LIBERO, reported as state of the art for that benchmark (Table 3).
Across real-world tabletop, mobile, and dexterous hand manipulation tasks, LaST0 improves mean success rates by 13%, 14%, and 14% over prior VLA methods (Table 5).
LaST0 reports a 14x inference speedup over explicit chain-of-thought VLA approaches (Section 1).

71122.text: RACO directly applies conflict-averse gradient descent to objective-specific pairwise preference losses instead of relying on explicit reward models (Section 3).
The clipped CAGrad update is introduced to stabilize multi-objective LLM alignment while respecting user-specified objective weights (Section 3.2).
The paper proves convergence of clipped CAGrad to Pareto-critical points that respect user-specified weights in nonconvex smooth settings (Theorem 3.1).
For two objectives, the analysis shows clipping can strictly improve the convergence rate (Theorem 3.2).
Experiments on multi-objective summarization and safety alignment across Qwen 3, Llama 3, and Gemma 3 report better Pareto trade-offs than reward-free baselines (Section 4).

F9NDKf5oPy.text: The paper formalizes masked diffusion sampling as an MDP in which the diffusion language model is the environment and the policy chooses which tokens to unmask (Section 3).
The learned unmasking policy is a lightweight single-layer transformer mapping token confidences to unmasking decisions (Section 3.2).
Policy sampling matches state-of-the-art heuristic samplers in semi-autoregressive block generation settings (Figure 4).
Learned policies outperform heuristic unmasking strategies in the full-diffusion generation setting (Figure 5).
Visualization of learned full-diffusion policies shows expert-steered policies recovering a left-to-right unmasking order on GSM8K samples (Figure 7).

XFTTezxLdU.text: Pretraining on Dyck sequences raises context-recall needle-in-a-haystack accuracy from 10% to 98% in the diagnostic experiments (Figure 2).
Front-loading 0.1% to 0.3% procedural data before natural-language, code, or math pretraining significantly outperforms standard pretraining (Figure 7).
Procedural pretraining lets models reach the same loss using 55%, 67%, and 86% of the original data on C4, CodeParrot, and DeepMind-Math respectively (Table 1).
Mechanistic transfer experiments find procedural pretraining affects attention and MLP layers differently across code and language domains (Section 6).
Experiments study combinations of multiple procedural-data forms as a path toward broader warm-start pretraining (Section 7).

fXr3uPr1G5.text: The paper proposes a unified QAT scaling law modeling quantization error as a function of model size, training data volume, and quantization group size (Section 3).
The scaling law is fit and evaluated using 268 W4A4 QAT experiments consuming 276K A100 GPU-hours (Section 4.1).
Quantization error decreases with model size but increases with more training tokens and coarser quantization granularity in the W4A4 setting (Figure 1).
Weight and activation quantization errors follow the overall W4A4 trend but have different sensitivities to training token count (Figure 5).
Activation quantization error in the FC2 layer caused by outliers is identified as the primary W4A4 QAT bottleneck, and mixed precision reduces that bottleneck (Figure 7).

Efq2VvYk1o.text: ThreadWeaver introduces a two-stage parallel trajectory generator for producing parallel chain-of-thought data for supervised fine-tuning (Abstract).
ThreadWeaver uses a trie-based rollout design to enable parallel reasoning on off-the-shelf autoregressive inference engines (Abstract).
The framework includes parallelization-aware reinforcement learning to balance reasoning accuracy with effective parallelization (Abstract).
On six math reasoning benchmarks, ThreadWeaver trained on Qwen3-8B reaches 79.9% on AIME24 and 71.9% average performance (Abstract).
ThreadWeaver reports up to 1.53x token-latency speedup while matching comparably sized sequential reasoning models (Abstract).

09CSjVeDug.text: DMPO fine-tunes diffusion LLMs by matching the model policy distribution to an optimal reward-tilted distribution through cross-entropy optimization (Section 3).
The method introduces weight baseline subtraction to make small-batch DMPO training effective (Section 3.4).
DMPO is trained without supervised fine-tuning in an R1-Zero-like recipe for reasoning tasks (Section 4).
Across evaluated reasoning benchmarks, DMPO consistently outperforms LLaDA-Instruct, LLaDA-1.5, d1, and cGRPO baselines (Table 1).
DMPO reports accuracy gains up to 54.3% over previous state-of-the-art baselines and 66.41% over the base model (Table 1).

ENuMNYCiV6.text: The paper proposes a meta-cognitive knowledge augmentation framework with Cognition-Guided Knowledge Expansion and Cognition-Driven Knowledge Calibration modules (Figure 2).
It reports a structural decay law linking higher answer accuracy to lower uncertainty across QA tasks and model families (Figure 1, Figure 7).
The full framework outperforms compared knowledge-augmentation and calibration baselines on diverse QA benchmarks (Table 1).
Ablations attribute performance gains to the proposed meta-cognitive assessment, knowledge expansion, and calibration components (Table 2).
CDKC improves confidence calibration and aligns subjective certainty with objective correctness across evaluated datasets (Figure 5, Figure 6).

PQaxfoEcRc.text: Mechanistic Data Attribution quantifies individual training-sample influence on targeted interpretable LLM units such as induction and previous-token heads (Figure 1, Table 3).
Targeted deletion or augmentation of high-influence samples causally modulates induction-head and previous-token-head emergence more than random interventions (Figure 2).
High-influence samples for induction heads are concentrated in repetitive structural domains, with top-ranked examples including LaTeX, HTML, and repeated text patterns (Table 1, Figure 4).
Synthetic data patterns selected from Pythia-14M attribution generalize to larger model scales when augmenting induction-head formation (Table 2).
Interventions that alter induction-head strength also shift in-context learning scores, supporting a causal link between the mechanism and ICL behavior (Figure 5).

LcswwEzzX7.text: AugE-Toolkit segments a source robot, inpaints the background, replays the trajectory with a target robot in simulation, and composites the augmented robot into the scene (Figure 1).
Scaling the number of augmented robot embodiments improves robustness on the source Franka robot under lighting and occlusion perturbations (Figure 2).
Simulation experiments evaluate how adding more augmented robots affects transfer to augmented robots and generalization to unseen robots (Figure 3).
OXE-AugE is built from selected OXE and additional datasets and expands the source demonstrations into millions of augmented trajectories (Figure 7).
Fine-tuning OpenVLA and pi0 on augmented Bridge data improves physical-task success on tested robot-gripper embodiments versus original Bridge-only training (Figure 4).

coHiGZOFtS.text: VenusBench-Mobile defines 149 primary tasks across 10 user-intent categories and 27 apps, plus 80 environment-variation tasks for stability testing (Figure 1, Figure 4).
The benchmark introduces the PUDAM taxonomy, scoring mobile GUI agents along Perception, Understanding, Decision, Action, and Memory dimensions (Figure 5, Table 6).
Its evaluation infrastructure combines Android-emulator interaction with hybrid verification using MLLM-as-a-judge and programmatic checks (Figure 6).
Evaluated mobile GUI agents show substantially lower success rates on VenusBench-Mobile than on AndroidWorld, exposing harder user-centric tasks (Figure 2, Table 3).
Stability evaluation requires success across original, Chinese, dark-mode, pad, and min/max setting variants, and reports low stability pass rates for agents (Table 4).

Hm8OEDKpiO.text: The OrthoMind-3D dataset combines programmatically generated in-domain scenes with out-of-domain game-engine and generative-AI scenes for block counting and object reasoning (Figure 2, Figure 6).
3ViewSense trains models in two stages: inducing canonical front/left/top orthographic views and then performing view-grounded reasoning with optional RL refinement (Figure 3).
On OrthoMind-3D, 3ViewSense improves block-counting and object-reasoning accuracy over evaluated VLM baselines (Table 1).
The method generalizes to out-of-domain OrthoMind-3D scenes and external spatial benchmarks better than the Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct base model (Table 2).
Ablations show that supervising view-grounded reasoning and using the two-stage SFT design outperform direct QA or incomplete training variants (Table 4, Table 5).

vKWxArobP3.text: AGSM formulates text-image alignment rewards with Plackett-Luce modeling and incorporates alignment guidance into score matching (Section 3.1, Section 3.2).
The method uses positive and negative soft tokens to adjust diffusion noise predictions toward aligned pairs and away from negative pairs (Figure 2, Algorithm 1).
AGSM improves T2I generation metrics on SD1.5, SDXL, and SD3 across COCO-val 5K and GenEval compared with baseline and SoftREPA variants (Table 1).
AGSM remains stable in later-stage training while SoftREPA validation ImageReward degrades despite lower training loss (Figure 4).
AGSM improves text-guided image editing trade-offs between alignment and structural preservation across PnP, MasaCtrl, and RF-Inversion settings (Table 2, Figure 5).

2hQBG2ZlFb.text: The paper categorizes SFT objectives by their token-probability gradient weights and positions them along a model capability continuum (Section 3, Figure 2, Figure 3).
At the model-strong end, prior-leaning objectives such as -p and thresholded NLL outperform standard NLL across the main evaluated models and datasets (Table 1).
At the model-intermediate region, prior-leaning and NLL objectives produce similar performance (Table 2).
At the model-weak end, NLL consistently outperforms the prior-leaning -p objective (Table 3).
Quantile-thresholding analysis finds low-probability tokens are harmful for model-strong settings but useful for model-weak settings (Figure 5).

KRSZj8z5Lr.text: LiME shares a single PEFT adapter and applies lightweight expert-specific modulation vectors instead of replicating a full adapter per expert (Figure 1).
LiME combines zero-parameter routing, adaptive expert selection, n-gram routing granularity, PEFT compatibility, and a shared trainable PEFT module (Table 1).
Average benchmark results report LiME variants as competitive with or better than MoE-PEFT baselines while using fewer total trainable parameters (Table 2).
Efficiency experiments show LiME variants achieve higher throughput, shorter training time, and up to 4x fewer trainable parameters than corresponding MoE-PEFT methods (Figure 2).
LiME's expert modulation is theoretically bounded as an approximation to expert-specific PEFT, and CKA analysis reports similar representations to MoELoRA (Theorem 2, Table 3).

A5venxSvpw.text: MASPOB constructs agent topology and prompt embeddings, predicts performance with a GNN surrogate, and selects prompts with a Linear-UCB exploration bonus (Figure 1, Algorithm 1).
Coordinate-ascent search decomposes multi-agent prompt optimization and is compared against exhaustive global search for accuracy and runtime (Section 3.3, Table 6, Figure 4).
Across HotpotQA, DROP, HumanEval, MBPP, GSM8K, and MATH, MASPOB reports the best or near-best mean accuracy among compared prompt-optimization methods (Table 1, Figure 2).
Replacing the GNN with an MLP reduces performance, supporting the role of topology-aware modeling in MASPOB (Table 3).
MASPOB generalizes to Qwen-3-32B as the backbone LLM under the same optimization settings (Table 4).

giNBsVVFGt.text: PRISM decomposes mid-training decisions across retention, domain interaction, benchmark selection, RL compatibility, and scaling behavior (Section 1).
PRISM mid-training improves code, math, and science benchmark averages across multiple model families compared with base checkpoints (Section Domain-wise Effects of Mid-Training Data).

Long-context restoration uses a base/mid-trained linear merge followed by long-context extension to recover RULER performance after mid-training degradation (Section Restoring Long-Context Ability After Mid-Training).
Weight analysis finds mid-training densely restructures model weights whereas RL makes sparse refinements (Section Weight-Level Analysis: Dense Restructuring vs. Sparse Refinement).

Applying RL after PRISM mid-training yields stable gains on code, math, and GPQA-Diamond benchmarks, while RL on base models shows limited progress on harder math benchmarks (Section Effects of Reinforcement Learning on Mid-Trained Models).

vSzRJyg6k0.text: RACO is an offline, reward-free preference-alignment method that accepts user-specified objective weights and explicitly handles conflicting objectives (Table 1).
The method uses CAGrad-Clip to limit correction gradients so updates better respect preferred objective trade-offs (Figure 1, Algorithm 1).
On TL;DR summarization, RACO achieves better Pareto frontiers for conciseness-quality and faithfulness-quality trade-offs than AMoPO and weighted-loss DPO baselines (Figure 2, Figure 3).
On BeaverTails safety alignment, RACO improves harmlessness-helpfulness Pareto trade-offs across Qwen3 and Gemma3 setups (Figure 4).
Ablations show clipping and the correction-radius constant affect validation margins and Pareto frontiers (Figure 5, Figure 6).

8m30ogkPk2.text: RoboMME defines 16 manipulation tasks organized by temporal, spatial, object, and procedural memory demands (Table 1, Table 2).
The MME-VLA suite evaluates symbolic, perceptual, and recurrent memory representations with multiple memory-integration mechanisms on a pi0.5-based architecture (Figure 2, Appendix A).
Main benchmark results show memory representation effectiveness is task-dependent across RoboMME task suites (Table 3, Figure 3).
Efficiency-performance analysis compares memory-augmented policies against baselines across success and resource metrics (Figure 4).
The benchmark includes real-world experiments in addition to simulated RoboMME evaluations (Table 4).

pl10b6EQAN.text: Program-of-Layers executes input-specific layer programs that can skip layers or recur over layers instead of using the fixed pretrained forward order (Figure 1).
MCTS-discovered execution programs improve DART-Math accuracy under depth budgets and often solve inputs with shorter unique layer depth than standard inference (Figure 3, Figure 4).
PoLar trains an end-to-end network to predict execution programs, avoiding expensive sequential MCTS at inference time (Figure 2, Section 3).
On LLaMA-3.2-3B-Instruct, PoLar improves pass@k over standard inference and dynamic-depth baselines across DART-Math difficulty levels (Table 2).
PoLar reports out-of-distribution pass@1 gains on Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B-Chat (Table 3).

KyVlaw4BxE.text: VideoFlexTok encodes a video as a flexible-length coarse-to-fine token sequence, allowing the same video to be represented with different token budgets (Figure 1, Figure 2).
The tokenizer uses temporal interleaving, register tokens, causal attention, and nested dropout to induce a 2D temporal/coarse-to-fine representation (Figure 3).
On Kinetics-600 class-to-video generation, VideoFlexTok is compared against 3D grid tokenizers on reconstruction FVD, generation FVD, and classification-score alignment (Table 1).
Flexible-length generation maintains comparable or better fidelity while using fewer tokens and improving conditional alignment on class-to-video and text-to-video tasks (Figure 7).
VideoFlexTok demonstrates 10-second, 81-frame text-to-video generation using 672 tokens (Figure 8).

VMsumctGvg.text: The paper compares image-based and action-based latent-action perspectives with four VLA supervision strategies: LA-Align, LA-Direct, LA-Cond, and LA-Tok (Figure 1, Figure 3).
On LIBERO, latent-action supervision strategies are evaluated against a unified VLA baseline and prior methods using success rate (Table 1).
On RoboTwin 2.0, the paper reports success-rate differences between the baseline and each latent-action supervision strategy (Table 2).
Real-world manipulation experiments compare model scores on four tasks with 10 rollouts per model-task (Figure 4, Table 3).
Ablations compare continuous embedding versus discrete-token latent-action supervision (Table 4).

HSuU4xBmAv.text: Top-W decoding selects token subsets by optimizing a Wasserstein-entropy-mass objective using embedding-induced geometry (Section 3, Algorithm 1).
The method instantiates a practical alternating decoder with an exact subset-update step inside a candidate-pool loop (Section 4.2).
Top-W is evaluated against Min-p, Top-p, and Top-H on GSM8K across multiple temperatures and models (Table 1).
Top-W is evaluated against the same decoding baselines on GPQA across multiple temperatures and models (Table 2).
Judge-based open-ended evaluations report Top-W wins on more AlpacaEval and MT-Bench temperature-model tuples than the compared decoding methods (Figure 1, Figure 2).

mDhyxu8WRb.text: mHC constrains hyper-connection residual mappings by projecting them onto a manifold to preserve stability relative to unconstrained HC (Figure 1, Section 4.1).
HC component ablations test the roles of pre, post, and residual mappings while maintaining dimensional consistency with fixed mappings (Table 1).
Training and propagation analyses show unconstrained HC has larger loss gaps, gradient norms, and residual propagation instability than mHC (Figure 2, Figure 3, Figure 5, Figure 7).
The paper introduces kernel fusion, recomputing, and communication-overlap infrastructure to reduce mHC system overhead (Section 4.3, Table 2, Table 3, Figure 4).
At 27B scale, mHC outperforms the baseline and surpasses HC on most zero-shot and few-shot downstream benchmarks (Table 4).

92oF5bU4cU.text: The paper argues that large pretrained models are surrounded by dense neighborhoods of task-specialized perturbations, unlike smaller needle-in-haystack regimes (Figure 1, Figure 2).
Solution density and diversity around Qwen2.5 instruction-tuned models increase with model scale (Figure 3).
Randomly sampled perturbations exhibit diverse task specialties rather than all acting as generalists (Figure 4).

RandOpt samples random parameter perturbations, selects top performers, and ensembles predictions; it matches or exceeds PPO, GRPO, ES, and related baselines in many LLM post-training settings (Algorithm 1, Figure 6).
RandOpt accuracy improves with population size and depends on sufficient pretrained model scale (Figure 7, Figure 8).

xEgoeNrp8B.text: PanoWorld-X generates controllable panoramic videos from a panorama image and an exploration route (Figure 1, Figure 2).
The Explorable Sphere-Aware DiT block combines exploration-aware attention for route control with sphere-aware attention for spherical geometric adjacency (Figure 2).
Quantitative evaluation compares PanoWorld-X with panoramic video generation and camera-controllable generation models (Table 1).
Qualitative comparisons show improved detail clarity and geometric coherence across generated panoramic keyframes (Figure 3).
Ablations evaluate the contribution of individual framework components (Table 2, Figure 5).

FneePKFVHT.text: PaperBanana is an agentic framework for generating academic methodology diagrams and statistical plots from source context and communicative intent (Figure 1, Figure 2).
PaperBananaBench contains 292 methodology-diagram test samples with source-context and caption statistics reported by the authors (Figure 3).
On PaperBananaBench, PaperBanana outperforms leading baselines on faithfulness, conciseness, readability, aesthetics, and overall score (Table 1).
Ablation studies evaluate the contribution of individual agent components to PaperBananaBench performance (Table 2).
For statistical plots, the paper compares vanilla Gemini-3-Pro, PaperBanana, code-based visualization, and image-generation approaches (Figure 4, Figure 5).

yVFxjNzCQm.text: PonderLM-2 delays token sampling by feeding the last hidden state back as the next-step input embedding, enabling latent continuous-space thoughts before emitting each token (Figure 2).
Parallel training uses Jacobi iteration to update latent hidden states in parallel rather than naively unrolling sequential latent thoughts (Figure 3, Section 3.2).
Scaling curves report that PonderLM-2-Pythia matches larger Pythia baselines with fewer parameters or fewer training tokens on the 300B Pile (Figure 1).
PonderLM-2-Pythia achieves lower language-modeling perplexity than same-size Pythia and larger vanilla Pythia baselines (Figure 4).
Zero-shot and five-shot downstream evaluations show average accuracy gains over corresponding Pythia baselines (Table 2).

jPKqiaPTEd.text: TEDBench is a large-scale non-redundant protein fold classification benchmark built from TED/AFDB predicted structures with an external experimental-structure test set (Figure 1, Table 1).

Masked Invariant Autoencoders mask a high ratio of backbone frames, encode only unmasked frames with an SE(3)-invariant geometric encoder, and reconstruct full-frame targets with a decoder (Figure 3).
MiAE benchmark results on TEDBench outperform or compete with supervised and pretrained protein-structure models across accuracy and macro-F1 metrics (Table 2).
Linear probing results isolate MiAE representation quality against models with more than 1B parameters (Table 3).

Ablations show high masking ratios, decoder design, reconstruction losses, masking strategy, model scale, and sequence incorporation affect TEDBench linear-probe performance (Figure 4, Figure 5, Table 5).

2RJN5vDHG0.text: The paper formulates LLM text generation as a stochastic process and adapts rare-event methods including importance sampling, reweighted distributions, and transition path sampling (Section 3).
Annealed transition path sampling generates biased text-completion trajectories that explore rare high- or low-observable completions (Figure 1, Figure 2, Algorithm 2).
MBAR reweighting reconstructs the true distribution of observables such as automated readability index from biased simulations (Figure 3).
Error analysis compares confidence intervals for MBAR rare-event estimates against direct sampling estimates (Figure 4).
Biasing toward readability uncovers rare completions far beyond the training-data quantiles and correlates with token repetition behavior (Figure 5).

trn64znfNx.text: WIRE applies rotary position encodings to graphs by using Laplacian spectral coordinates to define graph-dependent rotation angles (Figure 1, Section 3).
The WIRE transformation is equivariant to node-order permutations up to sign flips and rotations in degenerate eigenspaces (Lemma 1).
Regular RoPE is recovered as a special case of WIRE on grid graphs with appropriate learnable frequencies (Theorem 2, Figure 2).
WIRE asymptotically depends on graph effective resistance under the paper's spectral-feature assumptions (Theorem 3).

Experiments report WIRE improvements on synthetic monochromatic-subgraph and shortest-path tasks, point-cloud transformers, and efficient graph transformer benchmarks (Table 1, Table 2, Table 3, Table 4).

5VgZUEpK6W.text: Skill neologisms extend a model vocabulary with trainable skill-token embeddings while keeping pretrained model parameters fixed (Figure 2, Algorithm 1).
The method uses skill-centered datasets whose examples require the new skill composed with existing pretrained skills (Section 3.3, Figure 2).
Skill neologisms are compared with fine-tuning, LoRA, prompt tuning, and related approaches for skill-based continual learning properties (Table 1).
On digit-sequence transformation tasks, independently learned skill neologisms transfer to held-out two-skill and three-skill compositions (Table 3, Table 4, Figure 4, Figure A2).
Zero-shot composition of independently trained SHIFT and INV-POL skill tokens outperforms or complements in-context learning baselines in the reported setup (Figure 5).
A natural-language Skill-Mix experiment shows two separately learned skill neologisms can be combined at inference to elicit both target skills (Figure 7).

vIZz7LvObC.text: TokSuite releases 14 pre-trained language models that share initialization, architecture, data, and training budget while differing only in tokenizer choice (Figure 2).
TokSuite includes a multilingual robustness benchmark with 4,941 total examples across English, Chinese, Turkish, Italian, Farsi, Math, and STEM perturbation groups (Table 7).

The paper reports tokenizer-dependent relative performance drops under multilingual perturbations including input-medium, diacritic, orthographic, morphology, noise, LaTeX, STEM, and math perturbations (Table 1).
All 14 models converge to similar bits-per-byte values without loss spikes, supporting comparison of downstream differences as tokenizer effects rather than failed training (Figure 6).

2UH01A9Za0.text: DiReCT formulates annealing-stage sample selection as constrained optimization over per-sample gradients using Hessian spectral properties (Section 4.2).
The method imposes directional constraints so selected samples align with a curvature-aware descent path during LLM annealing (Section 4.4).
The flat-direction preference theorem states that the surrogate objective increases along sufficiently flat Hessian eigendirections under the paper's spectral regularity assumptions (Theorem 4.4).
DiReCT attains the highest aggregate annealing score among tested data-selection baselines at both GPT-2-Medium 355M and Llama-1.1B scales (Table 4).
DiReCT prioritizes high-loss, long-sequence samples under the paper's high-loss and short-length probing regimes (Figure 3).

OC2z7iSQKa.text: tau2-bench introduces a telecom dual-control environment where both the conversational agent and simulated user can act with tools in a shared dynamic state (Figure 1).
The telecom domain is modeled with separate agent and user databases, 13 agent tools, 30 user tools, and 114 sampled tasks from a 2,285-task full set (Table 1).
The benchmark uses a compositional task generator that creates verifiable telecom tasks from intent and subtask components (Section 3.2).
Agents show lower pass@1 in default dual-control telecom operation than in no-user and oracle-plan modes, isolating the cost of decentralized user coordination (Figure 4).
Telecom performance declines as the number of required actions or distinct issues increases (Figure 5).

BhahZSDowo.text: Critique-Resilient Benchmarking evaluates answers by treating an answer as correct unless an adversarial critique is upheld under bounded verification (Section 3.2).
The protocol admits generated questions through feasibility gating that rejects questions whose self-answer is successfully critiqued or whose question is ill-posed (Figure 1).
The ranking model jointly estimates answerer, questioner, and item effects with an itemized bipartite Bradley-Terry model (Section 5.2).
Answerer Elo scores correlate more strongly with external benchmark means than a baserate predictor in the reported Spearman and Kendall analyses (Table 1).
Train-set scores predict unseen question outcomes better than a baserate predictor in pooled log-loss and Brier score metrics (Table 2).

hgMZraPlSv.text: The paper formulates formal problem-solving as a deterministic Markov decision process and implements FPS inside formal theorem proving environments (Section 3.1).
Deductive Formal Problem-Solving decouples forward answer construction from optional backward proof validation for find-all problems (Figure 2).
FPS soundness is proved: any direct answer produced by FPS satisfies the formal problem predicate (Theorem 3.6).
D-FPS completeness and soundness for find-all problems are stated as formal theorems under the paper's conditions (Theorems 3.8 and 3.9).
The benchmark suite consists of FormalMath500, MiniF2F-Solving, and PutnamBench-Solving, constructed from informal and theorem-proving math benchmarks (Section 4.2).
The strongest evaluated baselines solve at most 23.77% of FormalMath500, 27.47% of MiniF2F-Solving, and 0.31% of PutnamBench-Solving (Table 1).

DK0kvnNelx.text: FlexRank factorizes each linear layer, obtains a global component ordering with dynamic programming, and distills nested submodels of different sizes from the base model (Figure 1).
The synthetic analysis shows post-training selection almost surely fails to recover optimal lower-rank submodels from arbitrary global low-rank minimizers (Theorem 4.1).
Nested subspace learning preserves nested minimizers for every rank in the synthetic matrix setting (Theorem 4.3).
FlexRank shows more graceful accuracy degradation than compared low-rank elastic baselines across LLM and ViT parameter budgets (Figure 4).
FlexRank submodels can be further fine-tuned with LoRA for math and code domains at multiple elastic sizes (Table 1).
Gauge-Aligned Reparametrization converts active-rank selection into measured forward-pass speedups on an RTX 5090 GPU (Figure 10).

lFkGJ60bGq.text: CLIP two-object scene embeddings are approximately reconstructable as sums of constituent object embeddings across text and image datasets (Table 2).
Object-level replacement in embedding space preserves intended probing and retrieval behavior for counterfactual scene edits (Table 3).
CLIP's binding function is high-complexity: approximators recover concept recognition on held-out objects but perform poorly on object recognition (Figure 4).
Controlled transformer embedding models trained from scratch achieve binding generalization on entirely held-out objects when training coverage is sufficiently high (Figure 6).
Multiplicative concept-interaction probes explain held-out-object binding better than additive probes in the controlled models (Figure 8).

syG9I9ofd8.text: LatentMAS replaces text-mediated multi-agent communication with auto-regressive latent thought generation and a shared latent working memory (Figure 3).
The paper proves latent thoughts can be more expressive than equivalent text reasoning under a linear representation hypothesis (Theorem 3.1).
Latent working memory preserves information equivalently to directly inputting preceding agents' outputs under the paper's formal setup (Theorem 3.3).
LatentMAS reports higher accuracy, lower output token usage, and faster inference than single-agent and text-based MAS baselines across six general tasks in the sequential MAS setting (Table 1).
On AIME, GPQA-Diamond, and other reasoning-intensive tasks, LatentMAS is evaluated under both sequential and hierarchical MAS settings with accuracy, token, and speed metrics (Table 2).
Input-output alignment improves downstream accuracy by 2.3% to 5.3% across three analyzed benchmarks (Figure 7).

yKcBAJMPXZ.text: MetaphorVU-Bench defines eight video-metaphor categories for systematic metaphorical video understanding evaluation (Figure 2).
The benchmark construction pipeline filters real-world short videos through multi-stage automatic filtration and manual annotation with quality control (Figure 3).
Current MLLMs perform far below a human-written upper bound on MetaphorVU-Bench, while reasoning-enhanced baselines provide limited improvement (Table 2).
Manual error analysis attributes MLLM failures mainly to missing, superficial, or improper cross-domain metaphor mapping rather than only wrong recognition (Table 3).
MetaphorBoost augments inference with a metaphorical knowledge graph and improves average scores for Qwen2.5-VL-7B, Qwen3-VL-8B-Thinking, and Gemini-3-Pro (Table 2).
Ablations show external metaphor-oriented graph knowledge is more effective than no external augmentation, plain text knowledge, or commonsense graph substitution (Table 4).

5PfEQzE9bf.text: The paper studies midtraining as distributional bridging that mixes specialized data with general pretraining data before supervised fine-tuning (Figure 1).
Controlled experiments pretrain Pythia-family models from 70M to 1B parameters on C4 for a fixed 128B-token budget before midtraining and SFT evaluation (Section 3.1).
Code-focused midtraining yields the largest gains on code tasks, math-focused midtraining improves math tasks, and mismatched midtraining provides little benefit (Table 2).
Proximity advantage between midtraining and target SFT data correlates with midtraining performance improvements across dataset pairs (Figure 3).
Midtraining mixtures outperform continued pretraining on 100% specialized data for tested code and math settings while preserving lower C4 validation loss (Table 3).
For code midtraining, early specialized-data introduction supports high mixture weights, while late introduction makes high mixture weights detrimental (Figure 4).

m1IRWFAMsa.text: NorMuon combines Muon's orthogonalized updates with neuron-wise adaptive normalization based on second-order momentum statistics (Algorithm 1).
The optimizer analysis shows Muon lowers update condition numbers but leaves high variance in per-neuron update norms, while NorMuon normalizes neuron contributions (Figure 1).
NorMuon achieves 21.74% better step efficiency than Adam and 11.31% improvement over Muon on the 1.1B pretraining setting (Table 1).
NorMuon also improves validation-loss trajectories over Muon and AdamW at the 5.4B scale (Figure 2).
On 5.4B training, NorMuon keeps optimizer-state memory close to Muon and below AdamW, with about 2.9% total training-step time overhead over AdamW (Table 2).
NorMuon outperforms Muon in Modded-NanoGPT pretraining at 124M and 350M parameter scales (Figure 5).

06Nk3dJDMq.text: The paper derives prompt steering interventions by subtracting unsteered activations from prompt-steered activations and trains PSR models to approximate successful prompt interventions (Figure 1).
Prompt steering applies highly token-dependent intervention strengths, motivating token-specific activation steering rather than constant coefficients (Figure 2).
PSR models estimate token-specific steering coefficients from activations and are trained with log-likelihood or MSE objectives to imitate prompt steering (Sections 3.4 and 3.5).
On Persona Vectors, all-layer PSR models outperform prompt steering at prompt-steering coherence for all three reported language models (Table 1).
On AxBench Gemma layer subsets, PSR variants improve over several rank-1 activation steering baselines and compare with multi-rank or multi-layer methods (Table 3).
Accumulated PSR interventions have lower relative RMSE to prompt-steering interventions than constant steering on the analyzed Persona Vectors data (Figure 3).

ds3ZOevkwx.text: MADQA contains 2,250 human-authored questions grounded in 800 heterogeneous PDF documents (Abstract).
The corpus spans 12.2M tokens across domains including financial, reports, government/regulatory, legal, HR, reference, and technical documents (Table 2).
MADQA is designed to include visual, structured-layout, tabular, and artifact-dependent questions rather than text-only document QA (Figure 4).
Agentic systems outperform static RAG baselines on MADQA, but an 18% oracle gap remains, indicating retrieval is a major bottleneck (Table 3).
Frontier BM25 MLLM agents can match human accuracy only at high step limits, while humans achieve much higher first-query accuracy (Figure 9).
Human searchers remain better calibrated across effort levels than MLLM agents under the Kuiper effort-accuracy calibration analysis (Figure 10).

RNuC8Nj6rD.text: TD3B formulates allosteric binder design as control over sequence-conditioned transition operators rather than optimization toward static conformations (Section 4.2).
The framework combines a target-aware Direction Oracle, a soft binding-affinity gate, and amortized fine-tuning of a masked discrete diffusion model (Figure 2).
The Direction Oracle achieves 0.93 accuracy, 0.90 precision, 0.91 recall, and 0.90 F1 for binary direction classification (Table 1).
TD3B obtains the highest gated reward among compared pre-trained, classifier guidance, SMC, TDS, and PepTune baselines (Table 2).
For targeted transition control, generated binders achieve 61% success for forward transitions and 100% success for reverse transitions under the paper's success definition (Table 3).
The paper evaluates TD3B-designed agonist and antagonist binders on GLP-1R and OX1R case studies (Figures 4 and 5).

GnqHK8Ww98.text: SOAR trains a teacher model with meta-RL to generate synthetic problems rewarded by measured improvement in a student model on hard target problems (Section 3.2).
The experiments target sparse-reward math subsets where the base model has 0/128 initial success on sampled hard problems (Abstract).
Students trained on SOAR promotion questions outperform hard-only training and intrinsic-reward teacher baselines on MATH and HARP fail@128 evaluations (Figure 3).
Grounded teacher rewards yield more stable student pass@32 trajectories than intrinsic teacher rewards across teacher seeds (Figure 4).
SOAR-generated MATH promotion questions recover 75% of the gains from full MATH training, while HARP promotion questions recover 50% of the gains from full HARP training (Section 5).
The final trained teacher policy does not improve direct inference on fail@128 test problems, separating generator utility from solver ability (Section 5).

kcyOjXoUZu.text: WALRUS is pretrained on 19 continuum-dynamics scenarios spanning astrophysics, geoscience, rheology, plasma physics, acoustics, and classical fluids (Abstract).
Patch jittering is theoretically motivated as a way to cancel aliasing artifacts in expectation under the paper's frequency-domain model (Proposition 3.1).
The training pipeline embeds 2D data into a combined 2D-3D space using singleton dimensions, zero padding, and symmetry-preserving augmentations (Figure 2).
Load-balanced distributed training buckets token counts to reduce deadweight in heterogeneous 2D/3D workloads (Figure 3).
After fine-tuning, WALRUS outperforms prior physical-dynamics foundation models on average one-step, short-horizon, and medium-horizon VRMSE metrics across downstream tasks (Figure 4).
The paper reports WALRUS achieves state-of-the-art results on 56 of 65 metrics across 26 tasks (Section 5.2).

IMFgiWw4jd.text: The ME2 principle characterizes reasoning traces along macro/micro granularity and efficiency/effectiveness axes (Figure 2).
The paper represents reasoning traces as DAGs with progression, branching, and merging structures for pairwise evaluation (Figure 3).
TRM is trained from a TRM-Preference dataset with a Bradley-Terry preference loss to score reasoning trace quality at scale (Section 5.1).
TRM reaches 88.6% accuracy on the validation-set pairwise preference evaluation, outperforming Qwen2.5-Math-PRM-7B, ReasonFlux-PRM-7B, and prompt-only judging (Table 1).
TRM-guided best-of-N test-time selection improves AIME24 and AIME25 performance over compared PRM baselines for GPT-OSS-20B and Qwen3-8B response models (Figure 4).
TRM-guided RL improves STEM and math benchmark averages over verifier-only RL, with the largest reported gains on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (Table 2).

BkMSFFtm5M.text: CVE-Factory transforms sparse CVE metadata into executable agentic vulnerability tasks containing instructions, environments, and verification tests (Figure 1).
The multi-agent pipeline uses six decoupling and coupling stages coordinated by an orchestrator with verification-triggered feedback (Figure 2).
Cross-validation against PatchEval reports 95.35% solution correctness and 96.13% environment fidelity pass rates (Table 1).
LiveCVEBench contains 190 tasks across 14 programming languages and uses more multi-container environments than Terminal-Bench or PatchEval (Table 2).
Fine-tuning Qwen3-32B on CVE-Factory tasks improves LiveCVEBench performance from 5.29% to 31.05% and Terminal-Bench from 12.50% to 31.25% (Table 3).
CVE-Factory achieves a 90.3% success rate in the workflow ablation, outperforming CVE-Genie at 48.4% and a Claude Code single-agent baseline at 0.0% (Table 4).

aIH1jyU37z.text: The arXiv paper introduces sheaf neural networks by replacing graph Laplacian diffusion with sheaf-Laplacian diffusion that can encode asymmetric, signed, and varying-dimensional relations (Section 3).
The sheaf diffusion operator is presented as a drop-in generalization of the diffusion operation used in graph convolutional networks (Section 2.1).
On synthetic semi-supervised node-classification tasks over signed graphs, sheaf neural networks outperform Kipf-Welling GCN variants across feature and edge-noise regimes (Figure 1).
The experiments average results over five random graph trials and report standard-deviation error bars for SheafNN and GCN comparisons (Figure 1).

wsA8LgHU5U.text: Learning-to-Theorize trains models to infer executable, compositional latent programs from raw observation pairs without direct program supervision (Figure 1).
Neural Theorizer infers a latent program by iteratively selecting primitives with a theory programmer and executing them through a shared transition model (Figure 2).
An MDL criterion selects the shortest accurate executable explanation among candidate program lengths at test time (Section 3.3).
On GridWorld, NEO and search-augmented NEO-S generalize to compositional and length-OOD settings where monolithic discrete and continuous baselines largely fail (Table 1).
On Arithmetic Factorization Reasoning, NEO-S substantially improves compositional-OOD and length-OOD transfer over monolithic baselines (Table 2).
Grounding loss, codebook size, and MDL weight each materially affect primitive recovery and OOD performance in the GridWorld ablation (Table 3).

iJwDylm93H.text: GUI-RobustEval contains 1,216 executable test cases targeting policy-induced GUI-agent error recovery (Table 1).
The benchmark evaluates recovery across four controllable error depths and reports both post-error success and error-awareness metrics (Table 2).
RoTS synthesizes error-recovery trajectories through explore-recovery co-expansion with fragility-driven exploration and experience-informed recovery (Figure 2).
RoTS-32B achieves 47.4% OSWorld success at max steps >=50 and 33.8% All-Pass@4, reported as state-of-the-art among compared GUI agents (Table 3).
Adding both fragility-driven exploration and experience-informed recovery improves GUI-RobustEval awareness/post-error success and OSWorld All-Pass@4 over parallel sampling alone (Table 4).
Scaling expansion rounds and dataset size improves RoTS success rate in the reported synthesis scaling analysis (Figure 5).

97NEP1pyS3.text: RLER maintains a fixed-size rubric buffer that is updated with rubrics generated from current rollouts and pruned by rollout-score variance (Figure 2).
DR Tulu-8B is trained as an open long-form deep-research agent using supervised cold start followed by online RL with asynchronous tool calls (Sections 4.2 and 4.3).
Across ScholarQA-CSv2, HealthBench, ResearchQA, and DeepResearchBench, DR Tulu-8B RL averages 65.6 and exceeds the best prior open baseline by 15.6 points (Table 1).
DR Tulu-8B lies on the performance-cost Pareto frontier and is reported as about 1000x cheaper per ScholarQA-CSv2 query than OpenAI Deep Research (Figure 1).
Evolving rubrics outperform using only initial search-based rubrics during RL training, with the gap widening over training (Figure 6).
Using Qwen3-8B as both judge and rubric generator still improves over the SFT baseline, though it underperforms GPT-based judging by 1.3 points (Table 4).

UamxHbDR3p.text: The paper formalizes text-driven amodal 3D generation, where text prompts steer unseen-region completion while preserving the observed input (Section 1).
RelaxFlow is a training-free dual-branch framework with an observation branch and a semantic-prior branch fused by velocity blending (Figure 3).
The relaxation mechanism is theoretically linked to low-pass filtering that reduces semantic vector-field estimation error (Proposition A.4).
The paper introduces ExtremeOcc-3D and AmbiSem-3D diagnostic benchmarks for evaluating extreme occlusion and semantic ambiguity in amodal 3D generation (Section 5).
RelaxFlow improves CLIP image/text scores, FID, LPIPS, and Point-FID over its TRELLIS and SAM3D backbones on ExtremeOcc-3D (Table 1).
RelaxFlow obtains the highest automatic CLIP scores and user-study preferences for alignment, 3D fidelity, and overall preference on AmbiSem-3D (Table 2).

AfqsNFzJcs.text: RGR-GRPO constructs rubrics from the input question and reference answer to provide dense reward signals during GRPO training (Figure 2).
The framework uses exploration assessment to trigger off-policy rubric-guided refinement only when on-policy exploration is insufficient (Figure 2).
RGR-GRPO improves over the verifiable online RL baseline by average margins of +7.0% on mathematics, +5.4% on physics, +8.4% on chemistry, and +6.6% on general reasoning benchmarks (Table 1).
The method is evaluated across 14 benchmarks spanning mathematics, physics, chemistry, and general reasoning domains (Section 3).
Ablations show rubric categories, off-policy shaping, and exploration assessment each contribute to average performance (Table 2).
The paper proves exploration assessment acts as a necessary adaptive variance controller for stabilizing RGR-GRPO training under its analysis assumptions (Theorem C.1).

7MlfE2Da2W.text: SCALE jointly modulates visual attention temperature and action decoding temperature using the VLA model's self-uncertainty (Figure 2).
The method requires no additional training, no verifier, and only a single forward pass per control step (Section 3.3).
With an OpenVLA backbone on LIBERO, SCALE improves average success rate over greedy decoding and compared sampling, top-k, top-p, and TTS baselines (Table 1).
With a pi0-FAST backbone on LIBERO, SCALE improves average success from 91.2% to 93.0% over the fine-tuned greedy baseline (Table 2).
On SIMPLER-WidowX, SCALE improves average success for pi0-FAST from 34.4% to 49.0% and improves SpatialVLA fine-tuned and zero-shot settings (Table 3).
Real-world pick-and-place experiments show SCALE improves average in-distribution and out-of-distribution success for both OpenVLA and pi0-FAST backbones (Table 5).

ATpOQt9VVd.text: OeMDM defines a generalized masked-diffusion NELBO that decomposes into a reconstruction term and a velocity-mismatch term for order-aware generation processes (Proposition 3.2).
OeMDM recovers autoregressive left-to-right modeling as a special case under a suitable scheduler (Proposition 3.3).
LoMDM jointly trains the diffusion backbone and learnable order schedulers from scratch with a single objective rather than post-training an unmasking sampler (Section 4.1).
LoMDM reports lower test perplexity than prior discrete diffusion baselines on LM1B and OpenWebText (Table 1).
LoMDM reports better zero-shot perplexity than MDLM on all seven evaluated transfer datasets and best diffusion results on most of them (Table 2).
The learned LoMDM scheduler improves generative perplexity relative to MDLM and to no-scheduler ablations across tested NFE budgets (Table 3).

GyRMbsYFiG.text: VGGT-Motion combines motion-aware submap construction, anchor-driven direct Sim(3) registration, and lightweight pose-graph optimization for calibration-free monocular SLAM (Figure 2).
Motion-aware submap construction uses optical flow to prune static redundancy and preserve turning segments for stable local geometry (Section 3.1).
VGGT-Motion improves KITTI absolute trajectory error over VGGT-Long and other foundation-model SLAM baselines under the paper's calibration-free setting (Table 1).
On long-sequence 4Seasons, Complex Urban, and A2D2 benchmarks, VGGT-Motion reports much lower ATE and drift than VGGT-SLAM and VGGT-Long while other foundation-model baselines often fail (Table 3).
Topology-aware turning encapsulation outperforms temporal slicing and parallax-triggered partitioning on KITTI ATE and drift (Table 5).
The runtime study reports large total-time speedups over VGGT-Long and VGGT-SLAM on long-sequence benchmarks (Figure 5).

ncRRCG4BfP.text: WestWorld introduces a knowledge-encoded embedding module and a system-aware mixture-of-experts block for trajectory world modeling across robot morphologies (Figure 1).
The model is pretrained on 89 complex environments spanning simulated and real-world robot data (Section 5).
WestWorld reports the best zero-shot long-horizon trajectory prediction errors against MLPEnsemble, TDM, and TrajWorld on Walker2D, Hopper, and Franka-style systems (Table 1).
WestWorld reports lower few-shot MAE and MSE than baselines on Cassie, A1, and UR5, averaged over three random seeds (Table 2).
Using WestWorld as the MPPI dynamics model improves accumulated reward on Walker2D, Hopper, and Unitree Go1 control tasks compared with evaluated baselines (Table 3).
Ablations attribute zero-shot gains to both the system-aware MoE layer and structural embeddings (Table 4).

fSnxuRhWoC.text: EOSTok jointly optimizes a 1D tokenizer and autoregressive generator so generation losses can supervise tokenizer learning end to end (Section 3).
The Autoregressive Prediction Reconstruction loss decodes teacher-forced AR predictions into pixel space to improve AR-predictable latent representations (Section 3).
EOSTok-H reports a guidance-free FID of 1.48 on ImageNet-1K 256x256 generation (Table 3).
EOSTok-L reports 1.74 guidance-free gFID with 312M parameters and 0.73 reconstruction FID for its tokenizer (Table 3).
Ablations report that semantic vision-foundation-model alignment improves 1D tokenizer convergence and reconstruction quality (Table 2).
Ordering and sequence-length ablations show that original 1D token order and moderate sequence lengths are important for generation quality (Tables 4 and 5).

Mkal0hTCnh.text: MEnvAgent uses a Planning-Execution-Verification multi-agent loop plus environment reuse via retrieval and incremental patching of historical environments (Figure 2).
MEnvBench contains 1,000 tasks from 200 repositories across 10 programming languages with execution support, quality assurance, and domain diversity (Table 1).
Across Kimi-K2 and Gemini-3-Flash backbones, MEnvAgent improves average F2P by 8.6 points, PASS by 11.0 points, and reduces time by 43.0% versus SWE-Factory (Table 2).
Removing EnvPatchAgent or environment reuse lowers reuse/pass rates and increases runtime in component ablations (Table 3).
Fine-tuning open-source coding models on MEnvData-SWE trajectories improves resolved rates on SWE-bench Verified and SWE-bench Multilingual (Table 4).
MEnvData-SWE contains 3,005 task instances and 3,872 solution trajectories across 942 repositories and 10 languages (Table 12).

OyPE1ganBR.text: Stable-GFN replaces explicit GFlowNet partition-function estimation with Contrastive Trajectory Balance based on pairwise trajectory comparisons (Section 4).
The method adds Noisy Gradient Pruning to filter uninformative reward differences under noisy red-teaming rewards (Section 4).
The Min-K Fluency Stabilizer penalizes non-fluent out-of-distribution prompts to reduce gibberish reward hacking (Section 4).
Stable-GFN reports stronger attack diversity and attack performance than GFN baselines across LLM red-teaming settings (Section 5).
Ablations evaluate loss-function and reward-stabilization choices, including the effect of reward constraints on attack discovery (Table 3).

WJcFtJriqv.text: UDM-GRPO treats the final clean sample as the policy action and reconstructs training trajectories with the diffusion forward process to stabilize GRPO for uniform discrete diffusion (Section 4.2).
Reduced-Step training optimizes three early high-noise timesteps to accelerate convergence (Section 4.3).
CFG-Free training removes classifier-free guidance during RL training while recovering and surpassing CFG-based quality after optimization (Section 4.4).
UDM-GRPO raises URSA GenEval overall score from 0.69 to 0.96 and reports state-of-the-art GenEval results among compared continuous and discrete T2I models (Table 1).
UDM-GRPO reports GenEval 0.96, PickScore 23.81, and OCR 0.57, improving over URSA and URSA without CFG (Table 2).
Ablations show final-clean-sample actions and forward-process trajectories outperform backward-trajectory variants on GenEval, PickScore, and OCR (Table 3).

8VVbElV06v.text: UniPercept-Bench organizes perceptual image understanding into Image Aesthetics, Image Quality, and Image Structure & Texture domains with Domain-Category-Criterion hierarchy (Figure 1).
UniPercept-Bench supports both Visual Rating and Visual Question Answering tasks for perceptual-level evaluation (Section 3.2).
UniPercept is trained with Domain-Adaptive Pre-Training followed by Task-Aligned RL for Visual Rating and VQA (Figure 6).
UniPercept outperforms compared MLLMs on UniPercept-Bench Visual Rating tasks (Table 1).
UniPercept is evaluated as a plug-and-play reward model for text-to-image post-training to improve perceptual attributes of generated images (Section 5.3.2).
The appendix defines ISTA in detail and compares UniPercept-Bench with other perceptual benchmarks (Sections 8 and 9.3).

ymHDVBwmta.text: AGoQ combines layer-aware activation quantization and precision-preserved gradient quantization within Megatron-LM-style distributed training (Section 3).
Layer-aware activation quantization reduces cached activation memory for a transformer layer from 28U in BF16 and 16.5U in COAT to 7.75U (Table 1).
Dynamic Bit-width Compensation for Pipeline Parallelism assigns higher activation bit-widths to underutilized pipeline stages while maintaining near-4-bit activation storage (Section 4.2).
Kernel fusion combines quantization/dequantization with adjacent GEMM operations to reduce activation-quantization overhead (Figure 4).
On LLaMA2-13B sequence lengths from 32K to 80K, AGoQ reports faster training than Megatron-LM and ZeRO-1 while avoiding activation recomputation in the listed settings (Table 2).
AGoQ reports lower memory than COAT and comparable or faster training time on OLMo-1B at 24K and 32K sequence lengths (Table 3).

75AYDsndHP.text: Autoregressive Boltzmann Generators replace flow-based Boltzmann generators with an autoregressive model that retains exact likelihoods and importance-sampling correction (Section 3).
ArBG avoids the invertibility/topology constraints of normalizing-flow Boltzmann generators and supports sequential inference-time interventions (Section 3).
ArBG reports improvements over flow-based Boltzmann generators across all evaluated molecular benchmarks, with especially large gains on 10-residue Chignolin (Section 4).
The paper introduces Robin, a 132M-parameter transferable ArBG model for molecular sampling (Section 4).
Robin reports more than a 60% reduction in zero-shot E-W2 energy error on 8-residue systems relative to the previous state of the art (Abstract).

MqzZ9X6m7f.text: The paper argues that compute efficiency alone is insufficient for sustainable open-source AI because lower per-run costs can increase aggregate derivative experimentation and deployment (Section 1).
The Data and Impact Accounting proposal standardizes carbon and water reporting metadata for model derivatives (Section 3).
DIA is designed as a lightweight transparency layer that integrates low-friction measurement into common training and inference pipelines (Section 3).
The position calls for public dashboards that aggregate impact reports across model releases and derivative lineages (Section 3).
The paper's central claim is that tracking only base-model impacts leaves cumulative open-source derivative footprints largely invisible (Abstract).

76XSBLdBdg.text: Hibiki-Zero trains simultaneous speech translation from sentence-level aligned speech data rather than word-level aligned interpretation data (Section 3).
Hibiki-Zero casts latency-quality optimization as reinforcement learning with GRPO over multistream speech/text outputs (Section 3.3).
The final Hibiki-Zero architecture is a 3B-parameter decoder-only multistream model built on RQ-Transformer audio token modeling (Section 4.1).
On Europarl-ST and Audio-NTREX-4L, Hibiki-Zero reports better long-form ASR BLEU, speaker similarity, and latency than Seamless, and improves over Hibiki on French short-form ASR BLEU (Table 1).
Human MOS evaluations rate Hibiki-Zero higher than Seamless on audio quality, speaker similarity, and speech naturalness across evaluated input languages (Table 2).
The model adapts to Italian-to-English simultaneous translation using 850 hours of fine-tuning data and reports Seamless-level quality/latency with better speaker similarity after RL (Table 3).

9wpwfSJCp9.text: SleepLM aligns multimodal polysomnography signals with natural language to support sleep interpretation and interaction beyond closed sleep-label spaces (Section 3).
The paper introduces a multilevel sleep caption generation pipeline for creating sleep-text supervision (Section 3).
The curated sleep-text dataset comprises more than 100K hours of data from over 10,000 individuals (Abstract).
SleepLM uses a unified pretraining objective combining contrastive alignment, caption generation, and signal reconstruction (Section 3).
SleepLM reports state-of-the-art performance on zero-shot and few-shot sleep understanding, cross-modal retrieval, and sleep captioning tasks (Section 4).
The paper demonstrates language-guided event localization, targeted sleep insight generation, and zero-shot generalization to unseen sleep tasks (Section 4).

gc7Gg18ejz.text: The paper proves tracking-error dynamics for a linear critic under non-stationary targets and connects stability to embedding covariance geometry (Theorem 3.1).
The analysis argues that isotropic representations equalize contraction directions and reduce drift amplification under a fixed variance budget (Section 3.1).
The paper motivates Gaussian representations because Gaussian higher-order moments are determined by covariance, limiting uncontrolled tail behavior (Section 3.1).
Sketched Isotropic Gaussian Regularization shapes learned representations toward an isotropic Gaussian distribution during RL training (Section 4).
On non-stationary CIFAR-10, adding SIGReg improves train accuracy AUC, feature rank, and dormant-neuron metrics across Adam, RAdam, and Kron optimizers (Table 1).
The empirical study reports that SIGReg reduces representation collapse, neuron dormancy, and training instability across evaluated RL domains (Section 5).

XztRm216YS.text: TimeRewarder learns dense proxy rewards from action-free passive videos by predicting frame-wise temporal distances (Figure 2).
The method converts predicted progress differences between adjacent frames into step-wise rewards for downstream RL (Section 4.2).
The paper provides a theoretical justification connecting temporal distance to progress-based reward shaping (Section 4.3).
On held-out expert videos, TimeRewarder reports the highest Value-Order Correlation among evaluated progress-based reward baselines (Figure 3).
TimeRewarder distinguishes successful and failed rollouts more coherently than VIP, Rank2Reward, and PROGRESSOR in qualitative reward/value curves (Figure 4).
On ten Meta-World tasks, TimeRewarder reports nearly perfect success in 9 of 10 tasks with 200,000 environment interactions per task (Abstract).

gz7hVnrRWq.text: The paper identifies performance plateaus, ineffective spontaneous self-reflection, and persistent failures as limitations of RL with only numerical rewards (Section 3.1).
Critique-GRPO trains from both initial responses and critique-guided refinements while combining numerical rewards with natural-language critiques (Section 4).
Critique-GRPO with CoT critiques improves average Pass@1 over R1-GRPO and R1-Dr.GRPO on Qwen2.5-7B-Base and Qwen3-8B across eight reasoning tasks (Table 2).
On Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Base, Critique-GRPO reports a 21.6-point average Pass@1 gain using 4K RL prompts and outperforms numerical-feedback baselines using 46K prompts (Table 3).
Self-critique Critique-GRPO improves Qwen3-8B average Pass@1 to 68.13 and AIME24 Avg@32 to 60.00 (Table 4).
Fine-grained ablations attribute gains to KL removal, language feedback, refinement sampling, and policy shaping, with the full objective reaching 47.08 average Pass@1 on Qwen2.5-7B-Base (Table 6).

z1bSFIEexL.text: Visual Information Gain is defined as a perplexity-based log-ratio measuring how much image conditioning reduces answer uncertainty (Section 3.2).
VIG is decomposable to sample and token levels, enabling fine-grained detection of visually grounded tokens such as colors, spatial relations, and attributes (Section 3.3).
Examples on MS-COCO show VIG is positive for matching images, smaller for partially grounded images, and negative for conflicting images (Table 1).
Token-level analysis identifies high positive loss differences for visually grounded words and near-zero or negative differences for weakly visual tokens (Table 2).
VIG-guided selective training prioritizes high-VIG samples and tokens to improve visual grounding while reducing supervision (Section 3.4).
Experiments compare VIG-guided selective training against full-data and existing methods for overall performance, data efficiency, and language-bias mitigation (Sections 4.2 and 4.3).

bYDjZyqKxq.text: MEMO optimizes inference-time context for multi-turn multi-agent LLM games by combining persistent memory retention with exploration through prompt evolution (Section 3).
The retention component stores structured insights from self-play trajectories in a memory bank and injects them as priors in later games (Section 3).
The exploration component uses tournament-style prompt evolution with TrueSkill-based uncertainty-aware selection and prioritized replay of rare or decisive states (Section 3).
Across five text-based games, MEMO raises GPT-4o-mini mean win rate from 25.1% to 49.5% and Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct from 20.9% to 44.3% using 2,000 self-play games per task (Abstract).
MEMO reduces run-to-run variance and yields more stable rankings across prompt variations (Abstract).
MEMO reports its largest gains in negotiation and imperfect-information games, while RL remains stronger in perfect-information settings (Abstract).

qiZDlnvWTR.text: NanoQuant formulates post-training LLM quantization as low-rank binary factorization with binary matrices and learned scales (Section 3).
NanoQuant is the only compared PTQ method marked as supporting both 70B+ LLMs and sub-1-bit compression (Table 1).
Across Llama, Gemma, Qwen, and Rnj model families, NanoQuant reports functional WikiText-2 perplexity at 1-bit and sub-1-bit settings where naive binary methods often fail catastrophically (Table 2).
NanoQuant reports competitive zero-shot commonsense accuracy against higher-bit binary PTQ baselines on Llama-3 and Qwen3 models (Table 3).
NanoQuant compresses Llama-2-70B from 137.95GB to 5.75GB, enabling the 70B model to fit within an 8GB consumer GPU memory budget (Section 4.4).
Latent-binary ADMM initialization outperforms Dual-SVID and DBF ADMM initializations for 0.8-bit Rnj-1 compression (Table 5).

XQlUqVCHJd.text: TimeSpot defines a joint geo-temporal benchmark requiring structured prediction of four temporal and five geographic attributes from ground-level images (Section 3).
The dataset contains 1,455 ground-level photos from 80 countries with broad season, daylight, month, continent, climate, and environment coverage (Table 2).
TimeSpot includes hemisphere sanity, hard OOD, geo-temporal fusion, schema, calibration, and verifiable GPS/OSM-style scoring axes absent from many prior benchmarks (Table 1).
Evaluated VLMs show substantially weaker temporal understanding than coarse geolocation, with top time-of-day accuracy far below top country accuracy (Table 3).
The benchmark reports that the strongest VLMs can reach 77.59% country accuracy while still incurring a median geodesic error of 892.54 km and low time-of-day accuracy (Section 1).
Supervised fine-tuning improves TimeSpot performance but remains insufficient for robust physically grounded geo-temporal reasoning (Section 5.4).

HwXyyvK7ZJ.text: VLM-RobustBench evaluates 49 augmentations, including 42 severity-based corruptions across nine categories and 7 binary transforms (Table 1).
The benchmark yields 133 corrupted settings per model-dataset pair by applying three severities to 42 corruptions plus seven binary transforms (Section 3.2).
The evaluation covers 11 VLMs from Qwen3-VL, InternVL3.5, Molmo2, and Gemma 3 families on MMBench and MMMU-Pro (Section 4.1).
Low-severity glass blur causes an average 8.1 percentage-point MMBench accuracy drop, larger than high-severity brightness reduction, illustrating a severity mismatch (Figure 1).
The study finds that spatial and resampling perturbations such as upsample and elastic_transform can cause drops up to 34 percentage points (Section 1).
Robustness is reported to vary by model family rather than simply by parameter count, producing family-specific vulnerability fingerprints (Section 1).

5kTn1c3vtt.text: Spectral Sphere Optimizer enforces module-wise spectral constraints on both weights and updates to realize a fully muP-aligned optimization process (Section 3).
SSO derives steepest-descent update directions on the spectral sphere and contrasts them with Muon and MuonSphere geometry (Figure 4).
SSO maintains constant activation magnitudes during Dense-1.7B training while AdamW produces substantially larger activation outliers (Figure 1).
